note: The write-window table of SDD 4.4, transcribed by hand from the document and never generated from the code. D-97 puts the table in the document so that the kill test enumerates it rather than inventing its own list; this file is that enumeration, and the test below refuses to run unless every row in it has a case. The design document is untracked in this repository (D-8), so nothing here can read it: what this file can promise is that no window is dropped from the list once it is written down, and that is said out loud rather than implied.
source: SDD 4.4, the windows a death can land in (D-97), as of SDD 1.19

windows.window: Status update written, commit not made
windows.answer: The criterion is the evidence and the recorded status is not: the job is re-checked and, where it passes, its commit is made at that boundary
head_commit is behind HEAD; the commit is the fact, the marker is reconstructed from it, provided the marker's commit is reachable

windows.window: Disposition decided, marker not yet carrying it
windows.answer: The disposition is written at the transition that decided it, so this window closes rather than being answered: a carried tour that died in VERIFYING used to reach closure as closed
All criteria pass and no report exists: the report is recorded as lost and closure continues from the block and .git
The entry still authorizes exactly one matching call; the authorization lapses at IDLE

windows.window: Closure commit made, baseline not refreshed
windows.answer: The next tour compares against the older baseline, which is stricter rather than looser

windows.window: Block cleared, closure commit not made
windows.answer: The cleared block is uncommitted in the tree; the tour log is the record, and the next closure commit carries it
